title: Written Claim Form for Lost or Stolen Cards, Paystride Visa Payroll Card Advantage
content:
The signed claim schedule for the Advantage plan of the Paystride Visa Payroll Card Account prices the provisional credit that posts when a cardholder whose card is on the Paystride Visa Payroll Card Advantage plan signs Paystride's written claim form. The form confirms a claim about a lost or stolen card that was first reported by phone.

## Claims within the schedule

The schedule prices the account's most recently registered claim of an unauthorized transaction handled under Regulation E error resolution that is under investigation, was first reported by phone, and has no written confirmation date. It prices that claim only when:

- it carries a loss date, the date the cardholder learned of the loss or theft;
- it carries no provisional credit;
- it is signed no more than 10 business days after its notice date;
- its loss's liability limit can be timed. The account's replacement orders placed less than 12 whole months before today must include at most one for a lost card and at most one for a stolen card, with exactly one of them placed on or after the loss date. That order's date is the day the loss was reported.

Orders placed 12 or more months before today never count. Under Paystride's program practice an account with repeated lost or stolen cards within those 12 months is referred to Paystride's card fraud review team, so the schedule books nothing for its claims. In every other case the schedule prices nothing and the base rule applies. Business days are Monday through Friday excluding Federal Reserve holidays, counted from the day after the earlier date through the later one.

## Effect of signing

When Paystride cannot complete a Regulation E investigation in time, it may take longer only by posting a provisional credit. For a signed claim this schedule prices, and only for such a claim, the provisional credit is the claim form credit, and it posts when the cardholder signs. The signing day is recorded as the claim's written confirmation date, and the claim remains under investigation.

The claim form credit is fixed only after every other claim of the same loss whose provisional credit stood above what that claim was due carries its reversal.

In other words, the claim form credit is not yet fixed while another claim of the same loss has a provisional credit standing above what that claim was due and no reversal of it shows on the account.

## Signing: `sign_card_theft_claim_form_2dc05390`

| | |
|---|---|
| What it does | The cardholder signs Paystride's written claim form confirming a claim about a lost or stolen payroll card on an Advantage plan, a claim given by phone, and the provisional credit for that claim posts with the signature. On success the claim records today's date as its written confirmation date, one provisional credit for the stated amount is added to the claim's payroll card account, and the card's available balance rises by that amount. The claim itself stays under investigation, and the cardholder sees the credit on the card right away. |
| Who runs it | The cardholder's own tool. The agent unlocks `sign_card_theft_claim_form_2dc05390` and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it. |
| `dispute_id` | The reference number of the card dispute (claim) the claim form confirms, as returned by the card dispute lookup for the cardholder's account. Identifier text. |
| `credit_usd` | The provisional credit amount the claim form confirms, in US dollars: a positive number with 2 decimal places. A value with more decimals is rounded half up to the cent before it posts. |
| Return | A confirmation line naming the provisional credit's transaction reference number, the dispute reference number, the credited amount in US dollars with two decimals, the written confirmation date (YYYY-MM-DD) and the card's new available balance in US dollars with two decimals. The transaction reference number shows the credit posted. |
| Errors | Nothing posts in these cases: `credit_usd` is not a positive dollar amount; there is no card dispute with that reference; the dispute is not a claim about a lost or stolen card (an unauthorized-transaction claim carrying a loss date); the claim was not given by phone; it is not under investigation; or the card is not on the Advantage plan. |
